Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Conversation, family & daily routines

look forward to verb and phrase

also looking forward to, look forward to seeing you, be excited about, I’m dying to know, be dying to, dying to know

classical

Caelius in Cic. Fam. 8.12.4: tē exspectō valdē
Cic. Att. 2.8.1: epistulam cum ā tē avidē exspectārem
Traupman 341

exspectō, exspectāre, exspectāvī, exspectātum

verb, first conjugation

look forward to, wait for, expect

The eagerness goes into an adverb: valdē, avidē, cupidē exspectāre.

Other words

  • aveō, avēre — long to, be eager to

    verb, second conjugation, with an infinitive; no perfect · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 1.15.2: valdē aveō scīre quid agās; Traupman 308

  • gestiō, gestīre, gestīvī, gestītum — be itching to, be dying to

    verb, fourth conjugation, with an infinitive · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 4.11.1: gestiō scīre ista omnia; Hor. Ars 159: gestit paribus conlūdere

  • nihil mihi longius est quam ut — I can hardly wait to

    with the subjunctive · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 11.27.1: nihil sibi longius fuisse quam ut mē vidēret

    “Nothing seems longer to me than (the wait) until …” (Lewis & Short s.v. longus).

Examples

  • tē exspectō valdē et quam prīmum vidēre cupiō

    I’m really looking forward to your coming, and I want to see you as soon as I canCaelius in Cic. Fam. 8.12.4

  • valdē aveō scīre quid agās

    I’m dying to know how you areCic. Att. 1.15.2

  • tum ille nihil sibi longius fuisse quam ut mē vidēret

    then he said he couldn’t wait to see meCic. Fam. 11.27.1

  • Valdē aveō scīre quid agās.

    I am dying to know how you are doing.Traupman 308

See also be itching to, wait, forward, wish.
